fields.h1: Build a Living Trust Form for Estate Planning Clients
fields.hero_description: Build a living trust form that gathers what the drafting attorney needs, with each client's answers in a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What the Form Asks Before Drafting Starts
fields.features_subheading: The form collects the facts. The attorney who drafts the trust decides what those facts mean under the client's state law.
fields.feature_1:
The grantor and the first trustee

The form opens with the grantor's legal name, county of residence, and marital status. It then asks who will manage the trust while the grantor is alive, by their full name.
fields.feature_2:
Successor trustees in ranked order

Clients name a first and a second successor trustee, each with a phone number and an email address. The attorney sees the ranking exactly as the client set it, first to last.
fields.feature_3:
Beneficiary shares that add up

Each beneficiary gets a relationship and a percentage, plus an optional backup if that person dies first. The form will not submit until the percentages total one hundred.
fields.feature_4:
An asset schedule with title details

For every asset, the client gives a description, an estimated value, and the name on the title or account today. The attorney can see which assets still sit in the client's own name.
fields.feature_5:
Deeds and statements read into fields

Clients upload a deed or an account statement instead of retyping it. The app reads each one into the asset schedule with AI, and a field read with low confidence goes to a person.
fields.feature_6:
Code your firm can take with it

Export the full code to your GitHub repository on paid plans. The intake can then run next to your client portal, and every later change lands in a repo your firm controls.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Clients, Four Kinds of Trust Work
fields.tab_content_1:
Every answer in before the first meeting

Walter Lindqvist opens the intake link from Kestrel Bay Estate Law before his first meeting. He names his daughter and then his brother as successor trustees, splits the estate among 3 beneficiaries, and lists 4 assets. Attorney Odile Fairbanks gets an email summary of his answers the moment he submits.
fields.tab_content_2:
Two separate trusts, chosen on page one

Nora Pell and Simon Achterberg are not married, and on page one of Harrow Lane Law Group's intake they pick two separate trusts. The form opens one property section per partner. Nora lists her condo, Simon his savings account, and both list the cabin at 27 Birch Row, which the app marks as co-owned.
fields.tab_content_3:
Ruth's two pending assets, each with a reminder

Ruth Calloway signed her trust on Sep 30, and Kestrel Bay paralegal Teo Marchetti tracks her asset schedule. Four of the six assets are now retitled in the trust's name. Her brokerage account and her car are still pending, and any asset pending after 14 days sends Ruth an email reminder.
fields.tab_content_4:
The parcel number goes to a person to check

Marcus Feld uploads the deed to his house at 418 Alder Lane instead of typing it in. The app reads the owner, the address, and the parcel number into his asset schedule. The parcel number comes back with low confidence, and paralegal Iris Bannerman checks it against the deed before the attorney sees it.

fields.howto_title: How to Create Your Living Trust Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to build a living trust form that collects what the drafting attorney needs, then publish it for clients.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Describe the intake in one prompt
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Add the asset rows and uploads
fields.howto_step_1_des: Ask your drafting attorney for the questions they put to a client at a first meeting, and pull the engagement packet your firm mails today. Mark which answers shape the draft and which only fill in names. That list becomes your prompt.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Write the prompt the way you would brief a paralegal: the sections, their order, and what each one asks. Emergent builds the form, the logic between its answers, and a database table for every intake, and you change any part later by prompting again.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Put the shared or separate choice on the first page. For separate trusts, have the form open a property section for each partner and flag any asset both of them list. A client filling it in alone never sees the second section.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Ask for one row per asset with its value and the name on its title, plus an upload slot for deeds and statements. Then set the confidence level below which a field read from an upload waits for your paralegal.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Alert the attorney on every submit
fields.howto_step_5_des: Have each submitted intake reach the attorney as an email or Slack alert with the client's name and meeting date. Ask for a reminder to the client 3 days before the meeting while the intake is still unfinished.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Test it with two sample clients
fields.howto_step_6_des: Fill the form twice: once as a widower with a house and a brokerage account, once as an unmarried couple choosing separate trusts. Open the database afterward and confirm each row holds the ranked trustees and every asset the client listed.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Have the drafting attorney approve the wording of every question before a client sees it. Then publish the form on your firm's custom domain, which Emergent includes and charges in credits, and link it from the engagement email.

faq_plan.q: What is a living trust form?
faq_plan.a: It is the document that sets up a living trust, or the questionnaire an attorney uses to gather what goes into one. The Bucks County, Pennsylvania Register of Wills defines a living trust as a trust that becomes effective during the lifetime of the settlor. Its glossary defines the settlor as the one who creates a trust of property.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a living trust form?
faq_plan.a: Describe it to Emergent's AI form builder in plain English: the grantor, the successor trustees in order, how the beneficiaries split the estate, and the assets going in. Emergent builds the form and a table for every client's answers. Ask the attorney drafting the trust to sign off on each question before clients see it.

faq_plan.q: Where can I find free trust forms to print?
faq_plan.ref: Where can I find free trust forms to print?

prov.original: Where can I find free trust forms to print?

faq_plan.a: Start with your state's law library. The Texas State Law Library says Texas has very few official legal forms and that you will not always find a free fill-in-the-blank form. It points to template books instead: its Texas estate planning e-book holds wills and trust forms in Volume 2, Part 5, and Texas residents can access e-books with a free library account.

faq_plan.q: Where can I get living trust forms?
faq_plan.ref: where can i get living trust forms
faq_plan.a: From the attorney drafting your trust, an online legal-document vendor, or a law library's template books. With an attorney, the intake comes first and the trust follows from your answers. Collect any sworn statement they ask for on its own affidavit form. A firm that builds its intake on Emergent keeps every client's answers in a database it owns.

faq_plan.q: Should an unmarried couple use a shared or individual living trust form?
faq_plan.ref: should unmarried couple use shared or individual living trust form
faq_plan.a: Either can fit; it turns on how the two of you own property. WillMaker's legal manual, written for a spouse or partner, says that if you own most of your property together, you'll probably want to make a shared trust. It names keeping sole control over your own trust property as a reason to make separate trusts. Ask an estate attorney in your state before you choose.

faq_plan.q: Where can I get a free revocable living trust form?
faq_plan.ref: where can i get a free revocable living trust form
faq_plan.a: On Emergent's free tier, if what you need is the intake side. The free tier covers building and publishing, which is enough for a firm to put up a free living trust form that collects each client's trustees and assets. The revocable trust document itself is then drafted from those answers by an attorney or from a template written for your state.

faq_plan.q: Do it yourself living trust forms?
faq_plan.ref: do it yourself living trust forms
faq_plan.a: Yes, you can draft from a template. In Texas, the state law library tells readers they may be able to draft their own custom form by using a form template or drafting guide. Pick one written for your state, and have a local attorney read the finished trust before you sign it. A firm that teaches a DIY trust workshop can take signups on a registration form.

flagged: PA6 asker unclear: fragment or name (no question word)
faq_plan.a: It is a living trust form for a trust the settlor can revoke. In California, Probate Code section 15400 makes a trust revocable by the settlor unless the trust instrument expressly makes it irrevocable. The section applies only where the settlor is domiciled in California at creation, signs the instrument there, or picks California law in it. Check your own state's statute.

faq_plan.q: How to fill out living trust form?
faq_plan.ref: how to fill out living trust form
faq_plan.a: Gather the facts before you open it: legal names, your successor trustees in order, each beneficiary's share, and every asset with the name on its title. Answer each section, then send the trust form to the attorney who will draft or review the trust. On an intake built with Emergent, each answer lands in the firm's own database the moment you submit.

faq_plan.q: Where to buy living trust forms?
faq_plan.ref: where to buy living trust forms
faq_plan.a: From an online legal-document vendor, or from an estate planning attorney who drafts the trust for a fee. Before paying, check which state's law the form follows and whether the price covers one document or a subscription. A firm that pays for software to run trust intake can reuse it for staff paperwork, such as an employee evaluation form.

plan.angle: The top 10 is legal-document vendors (LawDepot, LegalTemplates, eForms, USLegal) and fill-in trust PDFs from law offices and libraries: each hands one person one document. This page is for the person or firm drafting the trust. It builds the intake form that collects what the drafting attorney needs (grantor, ranked successor trustees, beneficiary shares that must add up, an asset schedule with how each asset is titled, uploaded deeds read into fields) and keeps every client's answers in a database the firm owns. It gives no legal advice: every legal statement is scoped to the one state or source that says it and quoted, and the attorney decides what the answers mean under the client's state law.
